title: Distinguishing pre-mRNA from mRNA in RNA-protein interaction studies
author: Zeiler, Bestehorn, et al.
materials: Thermo Scientific Pierce Anti-c-Myc magnetic beads
Thermo Scientific Pierce Protein A/G magnetic beads
Thermo Scientific NP-40 Surfact-Amps detergent solution
AppliChem EDTA Disodium salt 2-hydrate for molecular biology

steps.title: Decontaminate workspace and use sterile tips
steps.instruction: Clean the work area with an RNase decontamination solution and use only sterile filter tips for the entire experiment.

steps.title: Prepare inducible TTP‑expressing RAW264.7 cells
steps.instruction: Maintain RAW264.7 macrophage cells that carry a CRISPR/Cas9‑mediated TTP deletion and have been engineered to express C‑terminal Myc‑tagged TTP from a doxycycline‑inducible promoter.

steps.title: Perform RBP pull‑down and library preparation
steps.instruction: Metabolically label RNA, crosslink, immunoprecipitate the Myc‑tagged TTP‑RNA complexes, isolate RNA, construct sequencing libraries, and sequence the samples. Total duration is approximately 8 days.

steps.title: Enrichment analysis of TPM counts
steps.instruction: Using the TPM‑normalized count tables from pull‑down (PD) and Input fractions, execute the following computational workflow (≈1.5 h):

substeps.instruction: Calculate the mean TPM across all genes in the PD fraction; use this mean as a cutoff value.
Filter out genes whose PD TPM is not greater than the PD mean, retaining only genes with PD counts above the mean.
Verify filtering by confirming that the number of rows (genes) has decreased and low‑count genes are removed.
Log‑transform the filtered TPM values (add a pseudocount as needed) and discard any rows that yield non‑finite values (e.g., –Inf).
For each gene, perform a two‑sided t‑test comparing PD replicates versus Input replicates.
Adjust the resulting p‑values across all genes using the Benjamini‑Hochberg (BH) method.
Compute log2 fold change as mean_PD − mean_Input for each gene.
Classify genes as "enriched genes" if the adjusted p‑value equals 0; otherwise label them "not enriched genes".
Optionally, save the table of enriched/not‑enriched genes as a CSV file.
Create separate lists of genes classified as enriched in intronic counts and in exonic counts, then combine these lists into a single list of enriched genes.
